CATCHES: implementations that fail on grid-based layouts, have issues with
repeated patterns, or produce incorrect spacing for regular grid structures.

CATCHES: implementations that fail to handle minimal 2x2 rectangles at
the smallest possible size, produce zero or negative width/height values
when rectangle corners are immediately adjacent, emit invalid SVG coordinates
for degenerate cases, or fail to render rectangles that are only one cell
wide or tall after accounting for border characters.

CATCHES: implementations that fail to recognize Unicode overline (‾), macron (¯), 
en dash (–), em dash (—), and box-drawing horizontal line (─) characters, render 
them as text, or produce lines at wrong y-coordinates (not distinguishing between 
top-of-cell and middle-of-cell positions).

CATCHES: implementations that don't enforce the exact 3-value RGB requirement
for font colors, either using wrong color channels or crashing on incomplete input.

CATCHES: implementations where -c/--complex flag interacts incorrectly with
flipX, uses different character maps that aren't flipped properly, or applies
complex mapping after flip instead of before (wrong order) — arrow should point
left after flipX with complex charset.

CATCHES: implementations with off-by-one errors around threshold 129 — a pixel
with value 129 should activate dots when threshold is 129 (129 >= 129), but not when
threshold is 130 (129 >= 130 is false), proving the >= comparison operator.

CATCHES: implementations that only check some RGBA channels for negativity —
they'd allow negative blue or alpha while catching negative red, producing
corrupted color instead of validating all 4 channels must be non-negative.

CATCHES: implementations where custom character map is not preserved through
both flips, applies default map when flips are used, or maps characters incorrectly
after transformation — diagonal pattern should flip completely with both -x and -y.

CATCHES: PHP language feature regressions across the entire Zend engine test suite.
Each test verifies specific PHP behavior including:
- Type system and coercion rules
- Operator semantics (arithmetic, comparison, logical)
- Control flow (if/else, loops, switch, goto)
- Functions (declaration, calling, returns, references)
- Classes and objects (inheritance, interfaces, traits, properties, methods)
- Error handling (exceptions, error levels, handlers)
- Variable scope and lifetime
- Array operations and manipulation
- String operations and encoding
- Resource handling
- Magic methods and constants
- Namespaces and autoloading
- And many more edge cases

This test wraps the official PHP .phpt test format, executing the PHP code
in the --FILE-- section and comparing output against --EXPECT--, --EXPECTF--,
or --EXPECTREGEX-- sections. Tests with --SKIPIF-- conditions are skipped
appropriately.
Test anonymous function creation and execution.
Test error handler converting errors to exceptions.

CATCHES: incorrect MySQLi implementations that fail connection handling
(wrong host/port parsing, broken SSL negotiation, missing socket support),
implementations with broken query execution (incorrect multi-query parsing,
malformed prepared statement protocol, wrong parameter binding types,
buffer overflow in bind_result), implementations that mishandle result sets
(incorrect row count, wrong column metadata, broken fetch modes, memory
leaks in unbuffered queries), broken transaction semantics (autocommit not
respected, commit/rollback failing silently, wrong isolation levels),
implementations with incorrect character set handling (charset not applied
to connection, mojibake in escaped strings, wrong collation detection),
error reporting bugs (errno/sqlstate mismatch, missing error messages,
wrong error propagation in prepared statements), option handling failures
(MYSQLI_OPT_* constants ignored, wrong timeout application, broken local
infile controls), and implementations that crash on edge cases like NULL
parameters, empty result sets, oversized packets, or connection timeout.
